subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
School counsellor note. Dolma, Class 11. Self-referred, first session.
Dolma said she decided about two weeks ago that she wants to end things with Anirban, her boyfriend of five months. She hasn't told him. "He's not a bad person. I just don't feel it any more."
She listed reasons to wait: his birthday is next week; their friends are all in one group and "everyone will take sides"; she's scared he'll cry at school. Meanwhile, she said, he has been planning a surprise for their six-month mark. She twisted her sleeve while saying this and looked close to tears.
We talked about how delaying can feel kind but may add hurt, since Anirban is still hoping and planning. We discussed choosing a private time, face to face, and short, honest words. She wants to tell him after his birthday but before the six-month date. Will check in next week.

qa.q: How long has Dolma been with Anirban?
qa.a: Anirban has been her boyfriend of five months.

qa.q: Why has Dolma delayed telling Anirban?
qa.a: Dolma is afraid of hurting him, of friends taking sides and of him crying at school, so waiting feels kinder.

qa.q: What turning point did the counsellor help Dolma see?
qa.a: That the delay is adding hurt while Anirban plans a surprise; a private, face-to-face talk with short, honest words soon would be kinder.

qa.q: How might Anirban feel if he learns Dolma decided weeks earlier?
qa.a: Anirban might feel foolish and more hurt, realising he was planning a surprise for a relationship that had already ended in Dolma's mind.

grounding: Shows a teen who has privately decided to end a relationship but delays out of fear of hurting him and of friends' reactions, while he keeps hoping.

subtopic: A relationship's slow drift and breakup
passage:
Wednesday
It's been nineteen days since I knew. Standing in the canteen queue, Vinita laughing at something, and I just thought: I don't feel it any more. That was it.
And I still haven't said it. Every day there's a reason. Monday was her test. Today she sent me a photo of two movie tickets for Saturday with three hearts. How do you break up with someone holding movie tickets?
And the group. Ruksana has already asked why I'm "being weird". If I end it, everyone will have an opinion by lunch.
So I keep replying "haha yes" and "can't wait". Which is a lie. And every time I send one, she gets a little more excited, and I feel worse.
I think I'm not protecting her. I think I'm protecting me.
Rafiq

qa.q: What did Vinita send a photo of today?
qa.a: Vinita sent a photo of two movie tickets for Saturday with three hearts.

qa.q: What does Rafiq realise by the end of the entry?
qa.a: Rafiq realises the delay isn't protecting Vinita but Rafiq's own comfort, and it is making the guilt worse.

qa.q: What could Rafiq do before Saturday?
qa.a: Rafiq could meet Vinita privately before the film and tell her honestly and briefly, rather than letting her plan more around false hope.

qa.q: How is the delay affecting Vinita?
qa.a: Vinita keeps hoping and getting more excited, planning films and sending hearts, without knowing the relationship is already over for Rafiq.

grounding: Illustrates a teen who has decided a relationship is over but keeps delaying, fearing hurt and gossip, while the other keeps hoping.
